page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Breathing and Exchange of Gases · 2 marks

steps.label: What they are
steps.why: The twisted shape makes the air take a long slow path over a warm moist surface instead of shooting straight through.
common_mistakes: Calling conchae cartilages. They are bones.
Giving no number. There are three on each side.
steps.memory_tip: Conchae are the three scroll shaped bones in the nose.
steps.margin_note: Give the other name, turbinals, for a safe mark.
lines: Conchae, also called turbinals, are three
spirally twisted bones in the respiratory

steps.label: Their function
steps.why: Air reaching the alveoli must already be at body temperature, or the thin lining would be chilled and dried.
common_mistakes: Writing that they filter dust only. They condition the air.
steps.memory_tip: They warm the air before it reaches the lungs.
steps.margin_note: One line on the function is enough.

lines.text: They regulate the temperature of inhaled air
